sections.h2: Universal starter block (works across any chat app).
sections.html:
If you only install one portable instruction block across ChatGPT, Claude, Meta Muse, Gemini, Grok, or OpenRouter models, start with this compact 6-rule baseline. Notice every line defines observable output behavior rather than vague adjectives:

## Universal Communication Baseline - Start immediately with the direct answer, fix, or recommendation before background explanation. - Skip greetings, praise, prompt restatements, and closing offers to help further. - Separate observed facts from inference and mark missing data or unverified metrics as unknown. - Correct false premises upfront with concrete reasoning rather than agreeing smoothly. - Give one clear recommendation with key tradeoffs when I ask for a decision, unless I ask for options. - Keep routine replies scannable in under 150 words; expand cleanly when complexity requires depth.

faq.q: Which AI personality templates are highest leverage to copy first?
faq.a: Start with Meta Muse Soul.md (if using Meta Muse), Claude Personal Preferences, or ChatGPT Custom Instructions Box 2. Rules controlling answer-first ordering, explicit pushback, and unknown-fact reporting transfer across virtually every workflow.

faq.q: Should I replace my entire Soul.md or CLAUDE.md when installing a template?
faq.a: No. Back up your file first and append custom communication rules in a labeled section so existing safety boundaries, repository commands, or Muse core truths stay untouched.

faq.q: Can I use open-source AI system prompt templates in Ollama or OpenRouter?
faq.a: Yes. Open our OpenRouter & Open-Source Model Templates guide to pick your exact open-weight model (DeepSeek V4, Qwen 4 / 3.8, Llama 4, Mistral Large, GLM-5.3, Gemma 4) and export either a Markdown system prompt, OpenRouter API payload, or Ollama Modelfile.
